title: Application and admission
description: Willing to apply to the Bachelor in Communication? Read the admission requirements and discover if your diploma is accepted.

blocks.html:
Candidates who fulfil the academic requirements are invited to submit their application using the online form available on the page www.usi.ch/en/education-application.

Selection and outcome

USI Bachelor in Communication candidates usually receive the outcome of their application within 20 working days from the day they submitted their application. Please note that, in case of missing or incomplete documents, the review process may take longer.
This deadline may vary; we would ask candidates to follow the instructions they receive once they have submitted their application.

Good practice: navigate all the sections to discover everything you need to know about this programme.

items.title: Admission
items.html:
Holders of one of the following qualifications, obtained in Switzerland or abroad, are eligible for admission:

1. Swiss diploma (awarded in Switzerland or abroad)

Candidates holding one of the following educational qualifications have direct access to the Bachelor’s programmes of the Università della Svizzera italiana (USI):

  • Maturità federale and Maturità cantonale recognised by the appropriate Federal Commission;
  • Maturità commerciale cantonale (Scuola cantonale di commercio, Bellinzona);
  • Final diploma from a university of applied sciences or diploma of a technical college recognised by the appropriate federal authorities: in these cases, where the field of study selected is the same as the previous one, the single Faculties may recommend admitting candidates to an advanced level of the programme and exempt them from particular examinations or from the internship period.
  • School-leaving certificates issued by Swiss schools abroad are equally accepted.

2. Foreign diplomas

2.1 Admission requirements by country

The foreign qualifications recognised for admission to a Bachelor's programme at USI, as well as the admission requirements and conditions specific to USI applicable to candidates from each country, are published on the following website swissuniversities.

Applicants are therefore encouraged to verify that the qualification submitted for admission meets the specific requirements applicable to the country in which it was awarded.

2.1.1 Italian diplomas

Secondary education (or high school) diplomas conferred by the following types of schools are considered equivalent:

  • secondary school specializing in classical studies (liceo classico);
  • secondary school specializing in scientific studies (liceo scientifico); as well as secondary school specializing in scientific studies, applied sciences section (liceo scientifico, opzione scienze applicate);
  • secondary school specializing in foreign languages (liceo linguistico);
  • secondary school specializing in humanities (liceo delle scienze umane); as well as secondary school specializing in humanities, socio-economic section (liceo delle scienze umane, opzione economico-sociale).

The following secondary education diplomas are also considered equivalent:

  • secondary school specializing in art subjects (liceo artistico), limited to the Bachelor programmes in Architecture and in Italian language, literature and culture;
  • High school degree in Administration, Finance and Marketing (Amministrazione, Finanza e Marketing) conferred by a vocational high school (or trade school in economics), limited to the Bachelor programmes in Economics, Communication and Informatics;
  • High school degree in Informatics and Telecommunications (Informatica e telecomunicazioni), conferred by a vocational-technical high school, limited to the Bachelor in Informatics.

2.2 Admission requirements by foreign qualification

Applicants holding a International Baccalaureate, a European Baccalaureate or International Advanced Level + International GCSE are requested to verify the admission requirements specific to USI published at swissuniversities.

Applicants are also advised to consult the "Guidlines on Admission Requirements and Application Procedures for Bachelor's and Master's Programme".

Students who have, in another university or university of applied sciences in Switzerland or abroad, exceeded the number of failed examinations permitted by the Study Regulations, and have as a result been rejected by that university, shall not be admitted to study in the same Faculty or field of study (Admission and Matriculation Regulations, Art. 6).

items.title: Mature students (‘su dossier’)
items.html:
Candidates aged 25 or more, although not in possession of the required certificate of secondary education, may be admitted if their previous training and work experience (appropriately documented in their application file) is considered to be sufficient and relevant.

Following documents are required in order to submit an application:

  • Copy of a personal identity document (ID or passport),
  • Copies of academic qualifications (bachelor's degree, license, master's degree, high school diploma/school attendance certificate),
  • School transcript (only for candidates who obtain a high school diploma abroad),
  • Study plan (only for candidates who obtain a high school diploma abroad),
  • Certificate of Bachelor's/Master's exams (transcript),
  • Curriculum vitae,
  • Candidate's motivational letter,
  • Certificate of employment,
  • Italian/English language certificate (as specified in the Admission section of the program),
  • Certified translation of diplomas not issued in Italian, German, French, English, or Spanish,
  • Copy of the residence permit for foreign candidates already residing in Switzerland,
  • Certified translation of diplomas not issued in Italian, German, French, English, or Spanish,
  • Any additional documentation required by the form.

items.title: Language requirements
items.html:
For admission to Italian-taught Bachelor’s programmes at USI, a good command of Italian language is mandatory.

Which Italian-taught programmes require an official Italian language certificate?

For the following programmes, applicants whose native language is not Italian are required to provide an official Italian language certificate at the level indicated, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR):

  • Bachelor in Lingua, letteratura e civiltà italiana: B2
  • Bachelor in Comunicazione: B2
  • Bachelor in Scienze economiche: B2
  • Bachelor in Filosofia: B1

Which Italian language certificates are accepted?

The University accepts the following Italian language qualifications as proof of Italian proficiency:

  • CELI (Università per Stranieri di Perugia) – level CELI 3
  • CILS (Università per Stranieri di Siena) – level CILS Due
  • PLIDA (Società Dante Alighieri) – level PLIDA B2

Who is exempt from providing an Italian language certificate?

Applicants holding one of the following qualifications are exempt from providing an official Italian language certificate:​

  • A recognised Swiss upper secondary school leaving certificate (Maturità federale, Maturità cantonale or equivalent qualification according to USI Directives);
  • An upper secondary school leaving certificate obtained in Italy or at an Italian state or state-recognised school abroad;
  • A secondary school leaving certificate issued by schools in the Republic of San Marino;
  • Proof of having successfully completed at least 120 ECTS (Major) of Italian-taught coursework as part of a Bachelor's degree programme at a recognised university.

For programmes that do not require the submission of an official language certificate for admission purposes, it remains the applicant's sole responsibility to ensure that they have a sufficient command of the language to follow the courses effectively.

items.title: Conditional admission
items.html:
Applicants who have not yet obtained their upper secondary school leaving certificate at the time of submitting their application may be offered conditional admission to USI Bachelor's programmes.

Admission will be confirmed definitively only upon fulfilment of all outstanding requirements within the deadlines established by the Student Administration Service.

items.title: Required documents for the application
items.html:
To complete their application, applicants are invited to submit the following documents through the online application form available at www.usi.ch/en/education-application:

  • Copy of a personal identity document (ID or passport)
  • Copies of academic qualifications* (high school diploma / school attendance certificate)
  • School transcript (only for candidates who obtain a high school diploma abroad)
  • Study plan (see a sample here, only for candidates who obtain a high school diploma abroad)
  • Italian / English language certificate (as specified in the "Language requirements" section)
  • Copy of the residence permit for foreign candidates already residing in Switzerland
  • Certified translation of diplomas not issued in Italian, German, French, English, or Spanish
  • Any additional documentation required by the form
  • For foreign qualifications: documentation required in accordance with swissuniversities requirements

* while awaiting the high school diploma (or equivalent), the student must submit the school attendance certificate issued by the school

items.title: Number of available places
items.html:
Students with a Maturità federale and Maturità cantonale recognised by the Swiss Federal Commission are granted direct access to the Bachelor’s programme.
For the 2026–27 academic year, 150 places are available. Once this limit has been reached, a waiting list will be activated on a first-come, first-served basis.

items.html:

Late applications will be considered only in the case of available places.

items.title: Application fee
items.html:
Following cases are exempted from the application fee payment:

  • candidates with previous degree studies completed in countries signatories of the Lisbon Convention*

For those who are not exempted (see above), at the time of submission of the application form, a registration fee of CHF 100.- is required (application fee waiver is not possible).
The registration fee is non-refundable in the event of withdrawal by the student or rejection. In case of enrolment, the fee will be deducted from the first semester's tuition fees.

Mature student Bachelor applicants (“on dossier”)

The application fee for mature students (“on dossier”) is CHF 100.-, counting for the higher administrative costs of processing more complex files.
Exemptions are not provided.
Applicants by portfolio for the Bachelor in Architecture are invited to pay CHF 200.-.
Payment is not required for candidates of the Bachelor and Master programmes offered by the Faculty of Theology (affiliated to USI).

Payment methods

The payment through Saferpay is requested before submitting the application.
The application fee is non-refundable in the event of withdrawal by the student or rejection. In the event of enrolment, the fee will be deducted from the first semester's tuition fees.

*What is the Lisbon Convention?

The Lisbon Convention regulates the recognition of university degrees between signatory countries and considerably simplifies the administration of admission procedures.
For this reason, candidates whose previous degree studies were completed in countries inside this Convention (see list below), are exempted from the application fee.

items.title: Fraud warning / Security notice
items.html:
In order to better protect future USI students against potential fraud, we wish to draw attention to fake USI intermediary services and/or misleading advertisements on the Internet, as well as related board and accommodation/matriculation proposals.

USI has no intermediaries whatsoever in these roles.

Enrollment at USI can only occur when applications are validated by its Faculty admission officers or when submitted online - in Italian or in English - via the official website of USI. The latter offers all relevant information on admission requirements, procedures, fees and accommodation: www.usi.ch/en.

When in doubt, we strongly recommend:

  • To check and verify the identity of the intermediary;
  • Not to submit any personal documents or information;
  • To pay particular attention to messages written in languages other than Italian or English, which are the only two languages used by USI for all its official communications;
  • To be suspicious of any advance payment requests, as USI does not request advance payment of tuition fees and/or rent.

Please report any fake or fraudulent advertisements to USI: info@usi.ch.

USI shall take no responsibility for damages relating to incidents of this kind, to the use of such intermediary services, and to the acceptance of such proposals.
